content.title: Initiating Directive — INDOPACOM Theater Campaign Plan
content.summary: CDRUSINDOPACOM directs CJTF-WestPac to develop campaign plan for Western Pacific contingency operations. Tasking originates from INDOPACOM OPLAN 5077 and Global Force Management Allocation Plan FY26.
content.timeframe: FY26-FY28 planning horizon, immediate execution readiness NLT Q3 FY26
planningGuidance: Prioritize maritime domain awareness and sea denial capabilities in Taiwan Strait and South China Sea
Integrate allied/partner forces (Japan, Australia, Philippines) from outset of planning
Maintain escalation management options at every phase — graduated response essential
Plan for contested logistics in the Second Island Chain; pre-positioned stocks key
Assume degraded C4ISR environment; redundant communications pathways mandatory
constraints: Minimize civilian casualties in all COA development
Operations must comply with Law of Armed Conflict and ROE
Maintain freedom of navigation in international waters
restraints: No strikes on mainland China without SECDEF approval
Cyber operations above Phase 0 require CDRUSINDOPACOM approval
No unilateral operations in Japanese territorial waters without GOJ coordination

content.title: CJTF-WestPac Mission Statement
content.missionStatement: CJTF-WestPac deters PRC aggression in the Western Pacific; on order, conducts maritime operations to defend Taiwan and maintain freedom of navigation in the Taiwan Strait and South China Sea.

commanderIntent.purpose: Preserve the rules-based international order in the Western Pacific and defend Taiwan from forcible unification.
commanderIntent.method: Through integrated deterrence leveraging forward-deployed naval and air forces, allied partnerships, and information operations; if deterrence fails, through decisive maritime operations combining sea denial, air superiority, and distributed lethality across the First and Second Island Chains.
commanderIntent.endstate: PRC ceases aggressive military action, Taiwan's sovereignty is preserved, freedom of navigation restored, and the alliance network strengthened.

keyTasks: Establish persistent maritime domain awareness across the Taiwan Strait and South China Sea
Integrate JSDF, ADF, and Philippine forces into combined operational framework
Develop and maintain 3 viable COAs for graduated response from competition through conflict
Ensure logistics sustainment for 60-day high-intensity combat operations

content.title: Mission Analysis — Specified, Implied & Essential Tasks
specifiedTasks: Defend Taiwan against PRC military aggression (OPLAN 5077 Task 1.1)
Maintain freedom of navigation in the Taiwan Strait (FONOP directive)
Integrate allied forces under combined command structure (CDRUSINDOPACOM directive)
Establish air superiority within 200nm of Taiwan (COMAFFOR tasking)
Provide maritime logistics support to forward-deployed forces (OPLOG directive)
impliedTasks: Conduct ISR operations to establish maritime domain awareness
Pre-position logistics stocks at Second Island Chain nodes (Guam, Palau, Yap)
Establish redundant C4ISR pathways for degraded environment operations
Coordinate ROE synchronization with allied forces (Japan, Australia, Philippines)
Develop deception operations to mask force disposition and intentions
Establish cyber defense posture for critical C2 infrastructure
Plan humanitarian assistance for potential Taiwan civilian displacement
essentialTasks: Deny PLA Navy access to waters east of Taiwan (sea denial)
Maintain air superiority over the Taiwan Strait
Sustain forward-deployed forces for minimum 60 days of high-intensity operations
Preserve allied coalition cohesion throughout escalation spectrum

content.title: Facts and Assumptions Analysis

facts.description: PLA Eastern Theater Command has 3 amphibious brigades and 2 marine brigades positioned within 400km of Taiwan
PLAAF maintains 400+ 4th/5th gen fighters within combat radius of Taiwan
PLA Rocket Force has 1,200+ SRBMs/MRBMs capable of striking Taiwan and US bases in Japan/Guam
Japan has declared collective self-defense applicable to Taiwan contingency under 2015 legislation
US has 11 forward-deployed naval vessels and 2 CSGs within 72-hour response to Western Pacific

assumptions.description: Japan will grant basing access for US combat operations in defense of Taiwan
assumptions.validationIndicator: GOJ public statements and bilateral agreement status
assumptions.riskIfInvalid: Loss of critical forward operating locations; 40% reduction in sortie generation rate

assumptions.description: PRC will not employ nuclear weapons first in a conventional conflict over Taiwan
assumptions.validationIndicator: PRC nuclear posture statements, ICBM alert status, underground facility activity
assumptions.riskIfInvalid: Fundamental change to conflict calculus; potential strategic paralysis

assumptions.description: Australia will commit naval forces (2 FFH, 1 LHD) to coalition operations
assumptions.validationIndicator: ADF force posture, AUKUS readiness metrics, parliamentary authorization
assumptions.riskIfInvalid: Reduced maritime capability in southern approach; 15% gap in ASW coverage

assumptions.description: PRC will attempt cyber attacks on US/allied C4ISR within 48 hours of conflict initiation
assumptions.validationIndicator: Cyber threat indicators, APT activity monitoring
assumptions.riskIfInvalid: Underestimation leads to inadequate cyber defense posture

assumptions.description: Logistics throughput from CONUS to Western Pacific will be contested by PRC submarine and long-range missile forces
assumptions.validationIndicator: PLA Navy submarine patrols, ASBM deployment patterns
assumptions.riskIfInvalid: Over-reliance on contested sea lines of communication

content.crossReference: See DEMO-AGENT-OUTPUT-assumption-audit-01 for automated assumption validation analysis

content.title: Risk Assessment Matrix

risks.description: PRC pre-emptive strike on US bases in Japan before declaration of hostilities
risks.mitigation: Dispersal of forward forces, hardened shelters, integrated air and missile defense

risks.description: Allied coalition fracture under Chinese economic coercion
risks.mitigation: Pre-crisis diplomatic engagement, economic resilience planning, alliance solidarity messaging

risks.description: Logistics sustainment failure beyond Day 30 due to contested SLOCs
risks.mitigation: Pre-positioned stocks at Guam/Palau, alternative air bridge, expeditionary logistics concepts

risks.description: Escalation to nuclear threshold through miscalculation
risks.mitigation: Clear signaling, crisis communication channels, graduated response options, escalation off-ramps

risks.description: Cyber disruption of C4ISR causing loss of situational awareness
risks.mitigation: Redundant communications, mesh networking, degraded-mode procedures, cyber resilience training

content.overallAssessment: Mission is HIGH RISK. Principal risks are logistics sustainment and contested C4ISR. Mitigation plans reduce residual risk to acceptable levels for COA development. Coalition cohesion requires continuous diplomatic effort.

content.title: COA 1: Maritime Blockade
content.concept: Establish a naval blockade of the Taiwan Strait and key PLA Navy egress points to deny PRC naval access to waters east of Taiwan. Focus on sea denial through a combination of surface action groups, submarine barriers, and offensive mining.
content.mainEffort: 7th Fleet Surface Action Groups establish blockade line from Ryukyu Islands to northern Philippines, supported by submarine barriers in the Luzon and Miyako Straits.
supportingEfforts: COMAFFOR establishes air superiority umbrella with F-35 and F-22 from Kadena, Iwakuni, and Andersen AFB
Allied naval forces (JMSDF, RAN) secure southern approaches through Sulu Sea and Celebes Sea
3rd MEF establishes expeditionary advance bases on key First Island Chain positions for anti-ship missile coverage
Cyber operations degrade PLA Navy C2 and satellite reconnaissance capabilities

taskOrganization.mainBody: CTF 70 (3x DDG, 2x CG, 1x CVN), CTF 74 (4x SSN Luzon Strait barrier)
taskOrganization.supporting: JMSDF Escort Flotilla 2 (4x DD), RAN Task Group (2x FFH, 1x LHD)
taskOrganization.fires: 3rd MEF HIMARS batteries on Miyako-jima and Bashi Channel positions
taskOrganization.logistics: MSC resupply from Guam and Subic Bay auxiliary facilities

phasing: Phase 0 (Shape): Forward deploy forces, establish ISR coverage, pre-position logistics
Phase 1 (Deter): Show of force, establish maritime exclusion zone, diplomatic messaging
Phase 2 (Seize Initiative): Commence blockade operations, deny PLA Navy egress
Phase 3 (Dominate): Full blockade enforcement, offensive ASW, mine warfare
Phase 4 (Stabilize): Maintain blockade until diplomatic resolution
content.riskAssessment: MEDIUM-HIGH. Blockade is inherently escalatory and may provoke PRC kinetic response. Requires significant force concentration creating targeting vulnerabilities.

content.title: COA 2: Distributed Maritime Operations
content.concept: Employ distributed maritime operations across the First and Second Island Chains to create multiple dilemmas for PRC forces. Rather than concentrating forces for a blockade, disperse combat power across a wide arc to deny PRC ability to mass fires against any single node.
content.mainEffort: Distributed surface action groups (2-3 ship SAGs) operating independently across 6 operational boxes from Ryukyu to Palawan, each with organic ISR and strike capability.
supportingEfforts: Submarine force conducts independent offensive operations in PLA Navy operating areas
USMC expeditionary advance bases provide land-based anti-ship fires and forward arming/refueling points
COMAFFOR conducts distributed air operations from multiple hardened airfields across Japan and Philippines
SOF teams provide terminal guidance and intelligence from key observation posts

taskOrganization.mainBody: 6x independent SAGs (2-3 DDG each) with LRASM, 2x LCS with NSM
taskOrganization.supporting: 3x SSN independent patrols, JMSDF 4x DD in northern arc
taskOrganization.fires: USMC 3x NMESIS batteries, 2x HIMARS on mobile positions
taskOrganization.logistics: Expeditionary logistics nodes at 4 forward positions, resupply via small surface combatants

phasing: Phase 0 (Shape): Pre-position logistics, establish distributed C2 network, forward deploy SAGs
Phase 1 (Deter): Demonstrate distributed presence, show capability to deny maritime space
Phase 2 (Seize Initiative): Activate kill webs, engage PLA Navy forces in distributed engagements
Phase 3 (Dominate): Attrit PLA Navy capability, establish sea control in key areas
Phase 4 (Stabilize): Consolidate, transition to conventional deterrence posture
content.riskAssessment: MEDIUM. Dispersion reduces single-point-of-failure risk but complicates C2 and mutual support. Requires robust distributed C4ISR.

content.title: COA 3: Integrated Air-Maritime Defense
content.coaName: Integrated Air-Maritime Defense — Air Superiority First
content.concept: Prioritize air superiority over the Taiwan Strait as the decisive operation, enabling follow-on maritime operations. Concentrate air combat power to defeat PLAAF and establish a protective umbrella under which naval forces can operate with reduced threat.
content.mainEffort: COMAFFOR air superiority campaign using F-22, F-35, and B-21 from dispersed locations in Japan, Guam, and Australia to achieve air dominance over the Taiwan Strait within 96 hours.
supportingEfforts: Integrated Air and Missile Defense (IAMD) network protects forward airbases and naval forces
7th Fleet provides Aegis BMD and fleet air defense for CSG operating areas
Electronic warfare operations suppress PRC IADS and degrade early warning radar
Cyber operations target PLAAF C2 nodes and satellite ground stations

taskOrganization.mainBody: COMAFFOR 5x fighter squadrons (F-22/F-35), 1x bomber squadron (B-21), AWACS/tanker support
taskOrganization.supporting: 7th Fleet CSG with E-2D and F-35C for fleet defense, JMSDF AEGIS DDGs
taskOrganization.fires: THAAD and Patriot batteries protecting airbases, SM-6 from naval platforms
taskOrganization.logistics: Air bridge from Anderson AFB and Hickam, dispersed fuel and munitions caches

phasing: Phase 0 (Shape): Deploy air assets to dispersed locations, establish IADS network
Phase 1 (Deter): Demonstrate air superiority capability, CAPs and DCA over key areas
Phase 2 (Seize Initiative): Offensive counter-air and SEAD/DEAD to suppress PLAAF
Phase 3 (Dominate): Establish air superiority, enable naval operations under air umbrella
Phase 4 (Stabilize): Maintain air presence, transition to no-fly zone enforcement
content.riskAssessment: MEDIUM-HIGH. Dependent on rapid attrition of PLAAF; if air campaign stalls, naval forces remain vulnerable. High sortie rate demands robust logistics chain.

content.title: COA Analysis — Wargaming Results (In Progress)
content.methodology: Tabletop wargame with red team (PLA ETC) playing adversary most dangerous COA. Each friendly COA evaluated across 3 turns representing Days 1-7, 7-14, and 14-30.

strengths: Strongest deterrent signal — clear red line
Controllable escalation ladder — can tighten or loosen blockade
weaknesses: Force concentration creates targeting opportunities for PRC DF-21D/DF-26 ASBMs
Blockade requires sustained presence — logistics intensive
Legal/political complications of blockade enforcement on neutral shipping
keyFindings: Red team consistently targeted concentrated surface forces with saturation ASBM strikes in Turn 1
Blockade effectiveness degraded by 40% after Day 14 due to logistics strain
Most effective when combined with submarine barrier (hybrid approach)
coaResults.turnResults: Turn 1: Blockade established, 2 DDG damaged by ASBM. Turn 2: Blockade maintained but resupply contested. Turn 3: Blockade partially effective, coalition strain emerging.

strengths: Resilient to PRC massed fires — no single high-value target
Creates multiple dilemmas for PRC targeting
Best survivability profile across all COAs
weaknesses: Individual SAGs vulnerable to local PRC superiority
Difficult to achieve decisive effect — war of attrition risk
keyFindings: Red team unable to achieve decisive strike against any single node
Blue force C2 degradation in Turn 2 caused 30% coordination gap
Most effective at attrition but slowest to achieve campaign objectives
coaResults.turnResults: Turn 1: Distributed forces engaged successfully, minimal losses. Turn 2: C2 challenges, 1 SAG isolated. Turn 3: Steady attrition of PLA Navy, but no decisive engagement.

strengths: Fastest path to air superiority — decisive if successful
Enables all subsequent operations under protective umbrella
Plays to US technological advantage in 5th gen aircraft
weaknesses: High dependency on initial air campaign success
Airbase vulnerability to PRC ballistic missile strikes
If PLAAF not suppressed in 96 hours, campaign timeline collapses
keyFindings: Red team prioritized airbase attacks with DF-15/DF-16 in Turn 1 — 30% runway damage across 3 bases
Air superiority achievable by Day 5 IF dispersal and hardening adequate
Once air superiority established, maritime operations significantly less costly
coaResults.turnResults: Turn 1: Airbase strikes cause disruption, but dispersal limits impact. F-22/F-35 achieve 4:1 kill ratio. Turn 2: PLAAF attrited to 60% strength. Turn 3: Air dominance achieved, naval ops commence under air umbrella.
